st: Blend the chiles, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, vinegar, [[2 tsp]] salt and pepper into a loose marinade.
Cut along both sides of the backbone with kitchen shears and remove it. Press the chicken flat and slash the thick parts.
Rub two-thirds of the marinade all over and under the skin. Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Place the chicken skin-side up on a rack in a roasting pan.
Roast for 50 to 60 minutes until the juices run clear and the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F (74°C).
Brush with some of the remaining marinade during the last 10 minutes. Do not reuse marinade that touched raw chicken without boiling it.
Rest 10 minutes, then carve. Serve with the cooked sauce and rice or fries.
Put on gloves and stem the chiles. Chile oils can burn skin and eyes.
Add the chiles, garlic, lemon juice, vinegar, paprika, [[1 tsp]] salt and sugar to a blender.
Blend into a rough puree.
With the blender running, drizzle in the olive oil to make it smooth.
Pour the sauce into a small pan and simmer on low for 10 minutes to mellow the raw garlic.
Cool and pour into a clean jar. Chill for a day for best flavor. Keeps up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

ing: frozen, thawed, or collard greens finely chopped
st: If using collards, chop them very fine. Pulse in a food processor to get a mince.
Place the greens in a pot with [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cover and cook for 30 minutes until very tender, adding water if dry.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the onion mix and ground peanuts to the greens. Stir in the coconut milk.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick, stirring often.
Add the shrimp and the remaining salt. Cook 4 minutes until pink and opaque.
Serve hot with rice or xima.
Pat the shrimp dry. Mix half the garlic, the chiles, olive oil, lemon juice and [[1 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Toss in the shrimp and marinate for 20 minutes in the fridge.
Mix the melted butter with the rest of the garlic and the parsley.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan on high heat.
Cook the shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and curled.
Brush with the garlic butter and toss once more.
Serve at once with lemon wedges and rice.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook for 5 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the greens and a splash of water. Cover and cook for 10 minutes. Set aside warm.
Bring [[3 cups]] of the water to a boil with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] cornmeal with [[1 cup]] cold water, then whisk into the boiling water. Cook for 5 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the remaining cornmeal gradually, beating hard with a wooden spoon after each addition.
Cook for 8 minutes, turning and pressing the mass, until stiff and smooth.
Shape into mounds and serve with the greens relish.

ing: cooked crab legs or cleaned whole crab, cracked
st: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and [[1 tsp]] salt and cook for 8 minutes until they melt into a thick sauce.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the crab, spoon the sauce over it, cover and cook for 10 minutes to heat through. If raw crab, cook until bright red and opaque.
Taste and adjust salt. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with rice.

ing: black-eyed peas or red kidney beans, canned and drained
st: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs mostly clear. Drain.
Heat the oil in a pot and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat in oil.
Pour in the coconut milk, [[1.5 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Stir in the beans, reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 18 minutes.
Turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and serve.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water. Wait 5 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt. Add the yeast water and softened butter. Stir to a shaggy dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let it rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces and shape each into a tight oval roll.
Place on a lined baking sheet. Cover and let rise 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C). Place a pan of hot water on the bottom rack for steam, and slash the tops of the rolls.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding on the bottom.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes before serving.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 minutes until soft. Drain well and mash until completely smooth, then cool.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and line an 8-inch round cake pan.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the egg yolks one at a time, then the mashed potato and lemon zest.
Fold in the ground cashews, flour, baking powder and salt.
Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold into the batter in 2 additions.
Pour into the pan and bake for 40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes before turning out.
